title: 3/4 is also approached from above, giving an infinite descending sequence
body:
## The conjecture

The value 3/4 is an accumulation point of the scl spectrum of a free group from
above as well as from below, via

    scl = 3/4 + 1/(4m) = (3m+1)/(4m),

attained for essentially every m. Witnesses were found for m = 4 to 13, 15, 17 to
21, 23, 24, 25 and 27.

Two consequences. First, 3/4 is the first accumulation point from either side, and
the two families are symmetric about it:

    from below:  3/4 - 1/(2n) = (3n-2)/(4n)
    from above:  3/4 + 1/(4m) = (3m+1)/(4m)

Second, this answers the question of whether an explicit infinite strictly
descending sequence of scl values exists: the values above, taken in increasing m,
form one.

## What supports it

No value below 3/4 can be a limit from above, since that would require infinitely
many scl values in an interval below 3/4, where the computed spectrum is finite.
The minimum of scl - 3/4 over the sweep behaves like 1/(8L - 52) in the length L
swept: 1/44, 1/76, 1/92, 1/108 at lengths 14, 16, 18, 20.

The numbers here come from a computation carried out in an AI agent session in
August 2026 using `scallop`, in its rigorous exact-rational mode, and spot-checked
against two independent algorithms. **No person has checked it.** Treat it as
computational evidence and not as established fact.

What is missing is a single one-parameter family realising 3/4 + 1/(4m): by the
main theorem of *scl, sails and surgery* it cannot be a surgery family of fixed
shape, and every fixed-shape family tested increases rather than decreases. Since
the limit of a surgery family is the scl of the associated chain, the natural route
is a sequence of chains with scl decreasing to 3/4. Among all two-word chains of
total length at most 10 the smallest scl above 3/4 is 5/6, so that search has to go
further. Until such a family is exhibited, the descending sequence is a list of
witnesses rather than a construction.
